question.text: Scenario: Mr. Suresh Kumar, aged 40, works in the automobile industry and recently faced a salary reduction from Rs. 1,00,000/month to Rs. 75,000/month due to an industry slowdown. He has the following loans: (1) Home loan: Rs. 28 lakh outstanding at 9% p.a. fixed rate, EMI Rs. 28,000, remaining tenure 12 years; (2) Car loan: Rs. 3 lakh outstanding at 12% p.a., EMI Rs. 8,500, remaining tenure 3.5 years; (3) Education loan for son: Rs. 5 lakh at 10% p.a., EMI Rs. 10,600, remaining tenure 5 years. His non-debt monthly expenses are Rs. 35,000. He has savings of Rs. 4 lakh in FDs and Rs. 1.5 lakh in savings bank. His wife earns Rs. 25,000/month from tutoring. The bank has offered to restructure his home loan by extending tenure from 12 to 18 years at the same 9% rate, which would reduce the home loan EMI to approximately Rs. 22,000. Question 3 of 5: Using the stated restructured EMI of Rs. 22,000 over 18 years, the approximate additional total interest Suresh will pay over the loan lifetime (compared with the original 12-year EMI of Rs. 28,000) is closest to:

explanation.text: The Logic: Original total paid = Rs. 28,000 x 144 months = Rs. 40,32,000, so original total interest = Rs. 40,32,000 - Rs. 28,00,000 = Rs. 12,32,000. Restructured total paid = Rs. 22,000 x 216 months = Rs. 47,52,000, so restructured total interest = Rs. 47,52,000 - Rs. 28,00,000 = Rs. 19,52,000. Additional interest = Rs. 19,52,000 - Rs. 12,32,000 = Rs. 7,20,000, which is closest to Rs. 8 lakh. The Trap: Rs. 12 lakh would broadly correspond to a precise 9% / 18-year EMI of about Rs. 26,200 on Rs. 28 lakh (giving roughly Rs. 10.75 lakh of additional interest, closest to Rs. 12 lakh). With the stated Rs. 22,000 EMI, however, the additional interest computes to about Rs. 7.2 lakh. Note: The answer is sensitive to the restructured EMI assumed. Using the EMI as stated in the question (Rs. 22,000) gives an answer closest to Rs. 8 lakh; an exact PMT-based EMI on Rs. 28 lakh at 9% for 18 years would shift the answer towards Rs. 12 lakh.
